page.layout: One block of verse in a single column, headed by a title at the top; a catchword "Cedat-" at the lower right below the last line. No margin notes printed.

p.i: Quòd si Veteribus reddita olim patribus
Et ipsum amor paternus impediat suum
Tunc Iota supplex fundere, & puras Deo
Simul cateruis: corda quae is paludibus
Quas turpe quoduis praecipites agit ad scelus.
Sed hunc sequar quocunque mouerit pedes,
Spectare possim. Nam senex animum licet
Illum tamen per ima currens Vifcera
Quum stringere mucronem Volet, mirum nisi
Tot arietibus impulsa tunc ruat fides,

page.notes: Verse lines are rendered with line breaks; the original shows a few long-s and ligature forms (e.g. "Iota" for an ampersand-like flourish, "Volet", "Vifcera") that were read with uncertainty. The printed page has a faint mark at the upper left corner and show-through text, which were omitted.
